summary: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive space survival game designed to introduce children aged 7–12 to the challenges of human space exploration. Set in a simulated lunar or Martian outpost, players take on the role of mission managers and must manage essential resources, including oxygen, electrical power and radiation protection, to sustain their outpost. The game aims to incorporate NASA open data, particularly space-weather information, to introduce realistic environmental challenges into its gameplay. Developed using Roblox, the project combines resource management and interactive decision-making to make aerospace concepts more accessible to young learners. Through this experience, players can explore how astronauts and engineers plan missions, manage limited resources and respond to challenges beyond Earth.
details:
Our project is a Roblox-based space survival and educational game designed to introduce children aged 7–12 to the challenges of living and working in space. Players take on the role of junior astronauts at a lunar or Martian outpost, where they complete interactive activities such as wearing an astronaut suit, answering space quizzes, exercising, harvesting vegetables, collecting oxygen and mining stardust.

The game introduces important aspects of space exploration, including resource management, astronaut health and life-support systems. Players learn about equipment such as NASA's ARED, T2 and CEVIS exercise machines, which help astronauts maintain their physical health in microgravity. The project also explores how resources such as oxygen, food and electricity are essential for survival in an extraterrestrial environment.

The main benefit of our project is making aerospace and space science more accessible through interactive gameplay rather than conventional learning materials. We aim to encourage curiosity, scientific thinking and awareness of the engineering challenges involved in future human space exploration.

We developed the game using Roblox Studio and its Lua-based scripting environment. Roblox was selected because of its accessibility across multiple platforms, including computers, mobile devices and tablets, allowing more children to experience the game without specialised hardware.

What makes our project creative is its combination of educational content and resource-management gameplay. We considered the target audience's age, ease of navigation, accessibility and the balance between entertainment and scientific accuracy. We also referred to NASA resources and space-related research to ensure that the activities introduced in the game reflect real challenges faced by astronauts.
